Zhang Aman had always had shaky hands since childhood.
He couldn't hold onto the silver coins his parents gave him, nor the candied fruits from his friends. Anything placed in his grasp would inevitably tumble to the ground.
The onlookers would laugh, and Zhang Aman would laugh along.
But when he met that Woman, he stopped laughing. For the first time, Zhang Aman despised his own condition.
He handed her a bouquet, only for the flowers to scatter noisily across the floor; the sugar cakes he brought her, along with the porcelain Bowl, crashed onto the ground. The glistening sugar frosting smeared her skirt, making Zhang Aman's hands tremble uncontrollably with embarrassment.
The Woman laughed too, giggling as she pulled out a small needle case. With delicate fingers, she took out a few needles and asked Zhang Aman to close his eyes.
The needles gently pricked his hands, yet he felt no pain. The tingling sensation spread from his fingertips all the way to his heart.
When the needles were removed, the Woman's fragrance lingered three steps away from Zhang Aman.
It felt like a fleeting dream. When he awoke, his hands were steady again.
